chapter: Brawls, the Ink Spots and boyhood recollections
title: Highway work, school sweetheart and his family of eight children
summary: He recalls driving a mule on government road work, Mary Lucy at school, grocery delivery, his father's jobs, and being the only boy of eight children.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I told you about the mule with the light when I was working for the government. I had to strike a match to find my mule at 3 o'clock in the morning. I told you about that. And I told you about how the cart would pick up dirt and I got dumped on the dirt with a truck and all. And I told you about leaving there and going back to Louisville and I used to imagine all these years going and I ain't found a sweetheart. All these years gone by and I haven't found a sweetheart. I go back to school, you know, when I went back to Louisville, I started looking from nowhere and found one of the girls in the school, I'll never forget her, her name is Mary Lucy. She was a pretty girl. And I ain't tend my mind on no girls at all. I wasn't thinking about that. All this time I was working on how to make some money. How to make some money and I couldn't be worried about no girls when I'm looking to make some money, man. I got to do something. And that's what I'm busy doin'.

Oh, then I did this what's the name, in Louisville, I worked for what they call the Midtown Grocery Store. I used to deliver groceries from that grocery store. I'd drive a horse and wagon and my father used to work in Louisville Trust Company, firing boilers. He was an engineer-like, huh. That's in Louisville. And in Nashville when my father got the job there when I was going to school there before we were transferred to the 24th School in Indianapolis, my father worked for the Nashville Saddlery Company, you know. He died at the age of 47 -- 46 or 47.

And I had a good life. My family was good. I just loved my family. My mother was good to me. My father was good. My sisters were good. Had eight children, and out of eight children there was seven girls and one boy and I'm the only boy. So you can imagine how lucky I was, huh? 'Cause I was one they didn't want. But they couldn't get rid of me. That's the only thing about it.
